sections.h2: What kind of county is Bracken County, Kentucky?
sections.html:
Bracken County is a small, fully rural county on the Ohio River in northern Kentucky. Brooksville is the county seat, Augusta is the largest city, and Germantown is the third incorporated city. The county covers 209 square miles, with Clermont and Brown counties in Ohio across the river and Mason, Robertson, Harrison and Pendleton counties on the Kentucky side. It is part of the Cincinnati metropolitan area.

The county was organized in 1796 as Kentucky's 23rd county and took its name from Big and Little Bracken creeks. County government moved from Augusta to Woodward's Crossing, now Brooksville, in 1833. Burley tobacco was developed from Bracken County seed, and farming still shapes the land. The 2020 Census counted 8,400 residents, all living in rural areas, and the 2025 estimate is 8,511.

That small population means few sales, so a Bracken County seller should expect fewer nearby comparables than in a metro market. The PVA keeps the sales records that support assessments and appeals.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Bracken County housing?
sections.html:
The numbers below come from Census QuickFacts and cover 2020 to 2024 unless noted. Median home value is the lowest of the four counties in this part of Kentucky's guide set, and the commute is the longest.

Bracken County housing and work figures (source: U.S. Census Bureau QuickFacts)
MeasureBracken County
Median value, owner-occupied homes$125,000
Owner-occupied housing unit rate78.5%
Median gross rent$756

There were 3,839 housing units at the 2020 count, and 13.3 percent of them were vacant. Only 98 employer establishments operated in the county in 2023, so many residents drive out of the county to work.

sections.h2: Who do I call about a Bracken County tax bill?
sections.html:
The assessment and the collection are separate offices, both inside the county courthouse at 116 West Miami Street in Brooksville. The Property Valuation Administrator, at 606-735-2228, assesses your property, keeps the address and mailing name on the bill and handles exemptions. The Sheriff's Office, at 606-735-3233, only collects. Its office is on the courthouse's second floor.

  • Wrong address or name on the bill: use the return stub or call the PVA.
  • Question about assessed value: call the PVA before paying.
  • Prior-year bills: the County Clerk, 606-735-2952, because they must be paid there with a separate check from the current year.

The sheriff runs an online portal for viewing and paying bills. Card payments carry a 2.50 percent fee paid by the cardholder, and the sheriff receives none of it. Mailed checks must cover the full amount due.

sections.h2: When is the discount period for Bracken County property tax?
sections.html:
The sheriff's page gives the 2 percent discount window as October 1 through November 1. Bills are mailed directly to owners. After the discount ends, the face amount applies through December, and the standard Kentucky pattern of penalties follows in January and February through April 15. The sheriff's page lists only the discount window, so ask the sheriff's office for the exact later cutoffs on your bill.

Escrow is the usual trap. The sheriff sends a bill to the property owner and never to a mortgage company. If your lender pays your tax from escrow, forward the bill to the lender the day it arrives, or confirm that the lender has requested it directly. A returned check puts the bill back to unpaid status, and the repayment follows the schedule on the bill plus a bad check fee.

sections.h2: Why is a Bracken County bill sometimes in the previous owner's name?
sections.html:
Kentucky fixes ownership for tax purposes on January 1. If a house is bought after that date, the bill for that year is issued in the former owner's name, and the new owner receives nothing automatically in the mail. The PVA tries to reach new owners from recorded deeds. A buyer who misses the bill can ask the sheriff for a copy.

For sellers, this means a bill can arrive at an address the seller has already left. At the closing table, the settlement agent normally divides the year's tax by days of ownership and either pays the sheriff or credits the party who will. Give the closing agent a forwarding address for the bill.

sections.h2: How does a Bracken County owner challenge an assessment?
sections.html:
Ask the PVA for a conference first, because a county clerk will not take an appeal from an owner who skipped that step. The state calendar sets the real property tax roll open to the public for thirteen days from the first Monday in May. Appeals are filed at the clerk's office, and the deadline is the next workday after the inspection period closes.

When the PVA raises a value above what the owner listed, the owner must receive written notice under KRS 132.450(4). A paid representative must be an attorney, accountant, broker, appraiser or another qualifying professional with written authorization from the owner. Owners may record the board hearing on audio.

sections.h2: What happens to an unpaid Bracken County bill after April 15?
sections.html:
The sheriff transfers all unpaid bills to the County Clerk, who records a lien and files them as certificates of delinquency. The clerk sends the Department of Revenue a list by May 15, and the Department posts each county's list on its website by June 1. In a county on the normal schedule, a tax sale can be set for any business day from July 14 to August 28.

The county attorney mails a 30-day notice and a second notice that names the sale date. The clerk advertises the list in the newspaper with the largest paid circulation 30 to 45 days before the sale and posts it online at least 30 days ahead. Anyone who has not paid by the sale date risks having the lien assigned to a third-party purchaser, who may add its own fees.

Interest runs at 1 percent for each month or part of a month. In the state's worked example, a $1,000 bill reaches $1,254 when it leaves the sheriff and about $1,660 if paid after advertising in June.

sections.h2: Does Bracken County offer homestead relief?
sections.html:
Yes, for homeowners who are 65 during the year or permanently disabled. The Department of Revenue set the maximum exemption at $49,100 for 2025 and 2026. The home must be owned, occupied and kept as the personal residence on January 1, and the application goes to the PVA by December 31.

The sheriff asks eligible owners to call the PVA before paying a bill that shows no exemption, since a bill paid in full is harder to correct afterward.

sections.h2: How can I sell a Bracken County house that owes tax?
sections.html: List the tax as a closing item. Ask the sheriff for the current balance and the clerk for any prior-year payoff, then have the closing agent pay both from the proceeds. Inherited houses, houses with tenants, and houses that need more repairs than a retail buyer will accept often sell to cash buyers who take the property as it stands and pay the tax at the table.

faqs.q: What is the Bracken County PVA's phone number?
faqs.a: The PVA office in Brooksville answers at 606-735-2228. It handles assessments, mailing addresses on bills and homestead exemptions.

faqs.q: Where do I pay a Bracken County property tax bill?
faqs.a: Pay the sheriff at 116 West Miami Street, second floor, by mail, or through the sheriff's online portal. A card payment adds a 2.50 percent fee.

faqs.q: Does my mortgage company get my Bracken County tax bill?
faqs.a: No. The sheriff mails the bill to the owner only. Forward it to your lender if taxes are escrowed, or ask the lender to request it.

faqs.q: Where do I pay a prior-year Bracken County bill?
faqs.a: Pay it at the County Clerk's office, 606-735-2952, using a separate check from the current year's bill.

faqs.q: Who owes tax on a Bracken County house sold in the spring?
faqs.a: The bill goes to whoever owned the house on January 1. Buyer and seller normally split the year at closing and the agent pays the sheriff.
